Softly rolling orange desert extends around one compact rectangular Egyptian temple ruin. Massive pale sandstone walls rise as its dominant mass, slightly battered and broken into shallow projecting sections. Engraved panels, faded figures, hieroglyphic bands, thin gold accents, and turquoise, yellow, red, and blue painted friezes articulate the stone. Above, uneven pale stone coping encloses a flat, nearly complete slab roof.

The decorated entrance opens toward an open forecourt. A broad shadowed central opening, several closely spaced papyrus-style columns with colorful flared capitals, shorter square supports, and low painted railings reveal a dark columned interior and a faintly illuminated passage beyond. The other three elevations remain mostly solid and monumental, their surfaces repeating rectangular relief panels and horizontal ornamental courses.

In front and slightly to one side, four tall, slender painted columns preserve the remains of a detached colonnade. Two incomplete, offset sandstone lintel beams rest above their loose line, with obvious gaps and broken continuity. Around their bases, an irregular trail of cracked paving slabs and small fragments disappears partly into the sand, reinforcing the temple’s isolation in the vast desert.
